front: State the Doppler equation for blood velocity.
back: v = (c × Δf) / (2 × f_T × cos θ). Where c = speed of sound (1540 m/s), Δf = Doppler shift, f_T = transmitted frequency, θ = angle between beam and flow.

front: Why is there a factor of 2 in the Doppler equation denominator?
back: There is a double Doppler shift: once when sound strikes the moving RBC, and again when the RBC reflects sound back to the transducer.

front: When is the Doppler shift positive vs negative?
back: Positive (received > transmitted freq) when the reflector moves toward the transducer. Negative when it moves away.

front: Intracardiac Doppler shifts fall in the audible range of {{c1::~20 Hz to 20 kHz}}, even though transducer frequencies are 2–10 MHz.
Does Doppler measure speed or velocity? Why does it matter?
back: Velocity (magnitude AND direction). Doppler shift is signed — its sign tells us flow direction relative to the transducer.

front: At an intercept angle of {{c1::0° or 180°}}, cos θ = 1 and the measured velocity equals the true velocity.
What happens to the measured velocity when the beam is perpendicular (90°) to flow?
back: It is measured as zero. cos 90° = 0, so the Doppler shift is nulled.

front: Does a non-parallel Doppler angle over- or under-estimate the true velocity?
back: Underestimates it. Since |cos θ| < 1 for any angle other than 0° or 180°, the measured velocity is always less than the true velocity.

front: By convention, when performing Doppler how large an intercept angle is generally accepted before you correct or search a better window?
back: Angles up to ~20° introduce < 6% error (cos 20° ≈ 0.94); at 30° error is ~13%. Best practice is to keep the angle < 20°.

front: Which mode — spectral or color — reports peak velocity, and which reports mean?
back: Spectral Doppler (PW and CW) reports peak velocity. Color Doppler reports mean velocity (via autocorrelation of a packet of pulses).

Which mathematical technique is used by color Doppler to estimate mean velocity?
back: Autocorrelation. It is less accurate than FFT but much faster, making real-time color flow imaging feasible.

front: Why is a lower-frequency transducer preferred for pulsed Doppler when aliasing threatens?
back: For a given velocity, a lower f_T produces a smaller Doppler shift (v ∝ 1/f_T in reverse... shift Δf ∝ f_T). Smaller shifts are less likely to exceed the Nyquist limit.

front: In color Doppler, red = flow {{c1::toward}} the transducer, blue = flow {{c2::away}} from the transducer.
What does a green (variance) overlay on color Doppler indicate?
back: Variance in the mean-velocity estimate across the packet — flow disturbance, turbulence, or aliasing of high-velocity flow.

front: What is the mechanical index (MI) and why is it lowered during contrast studies?
back: MI quantifies the acoustic pressure (cavitation potential) of the beam. Lowering MI preserves microbubbles by reducing their destruction and enhancing harmonic resonance.

front: What is the thermal index (TI)? What tissue-heating threshold is used?
back: TI quantifies potential tissue heating. General guideline: keep tissue heating < 1.5 °C.
